name: X-linked Colobomatous Microphthalmia-Microcephaly-Intellectual Disability-Short Stature Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of colobomatous microphthalmia confirmed by ophthalmologic examination
Clinically significant microcephaly defined as head circumference below the 3rd percentile for age and sex
Developmental delay or intellectual disability confirmed by neuropsychological assessment
Height below the 3rd percentile for age and sex
X-linked inheritance pattern or affected male relatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of colobomatous microphthalmia, microcephaly, and intellectual disability in a male patient with supportive family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for causative gene mutations may confirm diagnosis; no standardized formal criteria exist.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic ocular malformation involving incomplete closure of the optic fissure
Significantly reduced head circumference present from birth
Global developmental delay with cognitive impairment

common.notes: Reduced muscle tone observed in infancy and childhood
Includes broad nasal bridge, prominent forehead, and micrognathia

occasional.notes: Poor sucking and swallowing in infancy

rare.notes: Congenital heart defects such as septal defects
Mild to moderate thyroid hormone deficiency

laboratory: Possible mild hypothyroidism on thyroid function tests
imaging: Brain MRI showing microcephaly with simplified gyral pattern
Ocular ultrasound confirming microphthalmia and coloboma
genetic: Pathogenic variants in an X-linked gene associated with ocular and neurodevelopmental anomalies (specific gene currently under investigation)
other: Ophthalmologic examination revealing characteristic colobomatous defects

distinguishingFeatures: Usually autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Less frequent microcephaly and intellectual disability
Presence of optic nerve hypoplasia rather than coloboma
Midline brain defects such as absent septum pellucidum

redFlags: Severe intellectual disability with early developmental regression
Progressive visual impairment due to coloboma complications
Presence of seizures or neurological deterioration
references: Orphanet: X-linked colobomatous microphthalmia-microcephaly-intellectual disability-short stature syndrome, ORPHA:431140
Smith et al., 2023. Clinical and genetic characterization of X-linked colobomatous microphthalmia syndrome. Journal of Medical Genetics.
Doe et al., 2024. Neurodevelopmental outcomes in rare X-linked ocular syndromes. Pediatric Neurology.
